item.title: Some of the first gameplay details for Grand Theft Auto 6 have been confirmed, and it seems like Rockstar is embracing a more RPG-y style this time around.
item.description: Some of the first gameplay details for Grand Theft Auto 6 have been confirmed, and it seems like Rockstar is embracing a more RPG-type style this time around. As part of a cover story for Dazed magazine, Rockstar Games revealed heaps of new information about Grand Theft Auto 6. Arguably the most notable details revolve around some of its gameplay features. In GTA 6, players will be able to eat, work out, and sleep, all of which have an impact on the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia. Players will have to take care of the Bonnie and Clyde-esque couple, as eating will affect their weight, working out will visibly change their build and strength, and a lack of sleep will negatively impact their features. It's unclear if a lack of sleep will impact the actual gameplay, or if they'll just look sleep-deprived, but it's a clear sign of Rockstar's attention to detail. For many, this may remind them of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. That game featured a lot of RPG mechanics that allowed CJ to fluctuate in weight and fitness. Later games largely dropped these elements, but GTA 5 featured a stat system that allowed players to enhance their stamina and strength by doing physical activities such as running, playing sports, and riding bikes. Additionally, there is also a social media feed for players to scroll, something fans have speculated about since the game's reveal in 2023. Character switching is also returning from GTA 5, allowing players to play as a couple or split up and operate independently. Dazed teased that the relationship between these two is a major focus of the game and that choices made by the player have "repercussions that cut much deeper" than the honor system in the Red Dead Redemption series.

item.title: Massive Entertainment, developers of Tom Clancy's The Division 2, announced a new DLC for the long-running online action-RPG/third-person shooter at a community panel at Gamescom. The new expansion is called Echoes of Central Park, and a full reveal will happen on September 24.
item.description: Massive Entertainment, developers of Tom Clancy's The Division 2, announced a new DLC for the long-running online action-RPG/third-person shooter at a community panel at Gamescom. The new expansion is called Echoes of Central Park, and a full reveal will happen on September 24. The Manhattan-set live-service game will finally head into Central Park due to a distress call from inside it. Echoes promises a darker tone wrapped in fear and mystery, with neither players nor their in-game avatars sure about what's inside or what Central Park has been like since the outbreak. Massive promises ample replayability for this DLC, including "a few twists" to give gameplay a unique feel. Speaking of gameplay, the developerse also want to lean heavier into gameplay here, rather than just new story content. Exactly how that will manifest itself remains to be seen. IGN gave The Division 2 an 8.5 out of 10 back in 2019 and the 2020 DLC Warlords of New York an 8 out of 10.

item.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend.
item.description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will be playable on Nintendo Switch 2 for free this weekend. Starting Friday, August 28 at 10 AM PDT, Nintendo Switch 2 players will have the opportunity to try Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for free. The beta's second weekend will kick off, giving Nintendo fans the opportunity to try a level from the game's campaign, multiplayer, and even the battle royale, Warzone. The Switch 2 version will boast unique features such as gyro controls, Joy-Con mouse controls, and, of course, being able to play the game on a handheld. Additionally, Switch 2 players will get free access to the game's Vault Edition content during the beta. This includes access to special skins, weapon blueprints, and more. Players can pre-load the beta on Switch 2 right now and pre-order the full game. It's the first time a Call of Duty game has been on a Nintendo platform since Call of Duty: Ghosts on Wii U. Nintendo fans have been wanting to see the franchise return to Nintendo hardware since then, but it hasn't been feasible until now. Digital Legends are developing the game's Switch 2 version after having helped develop Call of Duty: Warzone Mobile before its cancelation. The studio also did support work on the last two Black Ops games.

item.title: Extended gameplay footage revealing Grand Theft Auto 6's story prologue has been posted online, in a significant escalation of the past week's continued leaks.
item.description: Extended gameplay footage revealing Grand Theft Auto 6's story prologue has been posted online, in a significant escalation of the past week's continued leaks. More than four minutes of gameplay featuring GTA 6 character Lucia is now being spread over social media, in the first lengthy leak of footage that reveals key story details. If you are planning to try and experience GTA 6 with no narrative spoilers, now is the time to beware where you click online over the coming days and weeks. The footage's release comes just hours after Rockstar finally broke its silence over the leaks, which it called "heartbreaking" for its development team. In its statement, published online earlier today, the developer warned fans that spoilers would likely impact the manner in which it had hoped players would first experience the game — something that now appears to accurate. A fresh statement from the leaker, included as a watermark in this latest footage, makes several unsubtantiated claims about GTA 6's development, such as the game still being unfinished and that "too much" work remains on the game to be comfortably completed before the title's November 19 release date.

item.title: Xbox has revealed the price and release date for its 25th anniversary limited edition console, and it comes with a free game too.
item.description: Xbox has revealed the price and release date for its 25th anniversary limited edition console, and it comes with a free game too. Earlier this summer, Microsoft revealed that it will be releasing a translucent green Xbox Series X console, inspired by the original Xbox console, for the company's 25th anniversary. Now, Microsoft has confirmed that the console will cost a whopping $899.99 and release on November 13. It will come with the Xbox Series X console, a matching controller, and a free copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved. Pre-orders will open tomorrow, August 27, at 7 AM PDT. The controller can be purchased separately for $79.99, and it will release on October 20. If you're in the market for a brand new Xbox, this isn't a bad deal. The Xbox Series X itself costs $799.99 with a disc drive. This costs an extra $100 and includes one of Xbox's biggest games of the year. However, the next-generation of Xbox is also likely right around the corner. Microsoft confirmed earlier this year that it will detail its next console, codenamed Project Helix, later this year. It wouldn't be surprising if the next Xbox releases in fall 2027, as Microsoft has already indicated that will be a really important window for the company. The company also unveiled plans for a new disc-to-digital feature that will allow users to get a digital copy of their physical Xbox One and Xbox Series X games. It's been speculated that this is to prepare players for a transition to a more digital-focused next-generation console.

item.title: Xbox's new disc-to-digital feature is launching imminently, allowing users to add physical copies of games to their digital library.
item.description: Xbox's new disc-to-digital feature is launching imminently, allowing users to add physical copies of games to their digital library. The new feature will roll out to Xbox Insiders starting on August 31 before making its way to everyone at an unknown future date. This new initiative leaked earlier this summer and will be a way to allow players to put their Xbox One and Xbox Series X discs into their console and get a fully usable digital version. Your discs will also remain playable, but if you give the game to someone else and they insert that copy into their console, you will lose access to your digital license as well. It's not only great for the sake of convenience, but perhaps more notably, it also enables you to stream the game through the cloud or access it on other devices via Xbox Play Anywhere if the game supports those features. That means you don't have to have the game installed at all, and you can play it on PC, the ROG Ally, or even your mobile devices. Unfortunately, Microsoft made no mention of this feature being supported with original Xbox or Xbox 360 games, so don't expect those right now. Additionally, not every game will be supported off the bat. However, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said the company will support thousands of games when this feature launches, with more added over time. Will that eventually encompass Xbox 360 titles? It's hard to say.

item.title: Harry Potter movie star Rupert Grint will reprise his character of Ron Weasley next year, as he joins the Broadway cast of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.
item.description: Harry Potter movie star Rupert Grint will reprise his character of Ron Weasley next year, as he joins the Broadway cast of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. Grint is the second Harry Potter movie cast member to return to their childhood role for Cursed Child, the official J.K. Rowling-penned play that picks up the series' story years later, as Harry and Ron's children attend Hogwarts. Last year, Draco Malfoy actor Tom Felton returned as his fan-favorite Slytherin, supercharging interest in the Broadway production. Now, it seems like the play's producers are keen to pull off the same stunt again, with Grint also the right age to play Ron as a young father. "Ron Weasley has been a part of me since I was 11 years old and I can't wait to meet him again in this stage of life," Weasley said, via The Hollywood Reporter. "There is something so full-circle and so special about stepping back into Ron's shoes now when we are both fathers; it is somehow both very familiar and completely new. And the joy of being back on Broadway, this time in a role that defined so much of my life is truly exciting."

item.title: LEGO has unveiled an enormous new Star Wars Executor Super Star Destroyer set, which will soon become the company's longest model ever.
item.description: LEGO has unveiled an enormous new Star Wars Executor Super Star Destroyer set, which will soon become the company's longest model ever. While not the most expensive LEGO set or the model with the most bricks, the Executor's vast length will break a fresh record for the toy firm in terms of its length. At more than 136 cm long, this 6,130-piece Ultimate Collector Series model is one you'd need a very deep Dagobah swamp to hide in. Priced at a stonking $799.99 (£649.99), the set will become available on October 4, or via early access to LEGO Insiders from October 1. And if you need to measure up your home to find out if it'll fit, the set's dimensions will be 7.5 inches (20 cm) in height, 53.5 inches (136 cm) in length and 20 inches (50 cm) in width. Finally, it'll weigh just over 11 lbs / 5 kg. Which ship is the Executor? This is the super sleek, supersized Star Destroyer that Darth Vader uses as his flagship in The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi. Present at the Battle of Hoth and Battle of Endor, this ship is also the setting for Vader's meeting with various bounty hunters, included here as minifigures.

item.title: During our IGN gamescom Studio livestream, we were able to exclusively reveal the LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight Deluxe Edition - Mayhem Collection DLC trailer, which features an exciting look at the new story mission starring Harley Quinn and the Joker, the Mayhem Mode, and the Sinister Pack.
item.description: During the gamescom Studio livestream, IGN exclusively revealed the trailer for LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight Deluxe Edition - Mayhem Collection DLC, which features an exciting look at the new story mission starring Harley Quinn and the Joker, the Mayhem Mode, and the Sinister Pack. LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight's Mayhem Collection DLC will be available to all Deluxe Edition owners for no extra cost on September 18, 2026, the same day the game launches on Nintendo Switch 2. The big addition in the DLC is that new story mission that stars Harley Quinn and The Joker, which will see the pair working together to "orchestrate a breakout from Arkham Asylum with a going-away party Gotham City won't soon forget." Harley Quinn will be equipped with her trusty hammer and her Fun Gun loaded with Confetti and Bubblegum, and she'll also be able to summon her beloved hyenas, Bud and Lou. As for the Joker, he'll bring his Paintball Pelter and Boxing Glove to the party alongside a "fast-paced, agile combat style that is focused on speed and mobility." Players will also be able to unlock outfits for Harley Quinn and the Joker that are based on past Batman Media, including The Dark Knight Returns comic book series, Batman: The Animated Series, and more.

item.title: Rockstar Games has finally addressed the past week's extraordinary spate of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks.
item.description: Rockstar Games has finally addressed the past week's extraordinary spate of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. In a statement posted to social media, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19. The past week has seen more than a dozen gameplay clips appear online, posted by an individual or group that has claimed to be leaking material to highlight the death of physical media and the impact this will have on game ownership, while also charging fans to vote on further leaks using cryptocurrency, in what is widely-seen as a money-making exercise. Today's statement by Rockstar makes no mention of its efforts to try and stop these leaks from occuring, or the legal processes it has begun to try and determine the identity of the leaker(s). Indeed, the statement could be read as an admission that the leaks will likely continue — and worsen, with story spoilers likely — at least in the short term.

item.title: We all love Avengers: Endgame, but some Marvel fans are now suggesting that the four minutes of footage added to its upcoming Encore re-release risk being oversold by its directors.
item.description: We all love Avengers: Endgame, but some Marvel fans are now suggesting that the four minutes of footage added to its upcoming Encore re-release risk being oversold by its directors. Endgame is one of the best Marvel movies of all time — perhaps the best — and so it's not surprising to see it return to theaters this fall ahead of Avengers: Doomsday's arrival. Not only will this new chance to watch the film inject a few more million into its box office total (perhaps enough to overtake Avatar once again!), the experience will likely remind cinema audiences of the excitement felt at the close of the Infinity Saga, as a decade of storytelling came to a natural conclusion. But after the reveal that Avengers: Endgame Encore will be just four minutes longer than the movie's original runtime, fans are revisiting recent comments by directors Joe and Anthony Russo — who suggested that an Endgame watch (or rewatch) was "required viewing" to follow Doomsday's own story — with a healthy dose of scepticism. A clip of the Russos discussing Avengers: Endgame Encore at San Diego Comic-Con last month is now being shared widely on social media, where the duo discussed why they thought fans should see the film again with Fandango.

item.title: IKEA has unveiled a range of official Xbox furniture, including gaming chairs, display stands and cozy-looking D-pad cushion.
item.description: IKEA has unveiled a range of official Xbox furniture, including gaming chairs, display stands and cozy-looking D-pad cushions. The range goes on sale in the U.K. from October via the retailer's website and in IKEA stores, and is officially named "YXSTABY" — a name I won't try and pronounce out loud. In a press release sent to IGN today, IKEA said that YXSTABY reflected "an era where gaming furniture is moving out of teen bedrooms and man caves and into the mainstream living room." Created together by Xbox and IKEA designers, the nine-piece collection includes functional furniture such as controller display boxes, TV stands on castors, and a side table to store all your gaming accessories.

item.title: LEGO has finally revealed its Super Mario range that will include minifigures for the first time, including playsets for Bowser's Castle and numerous Mario Kart vehicles.
item.description: LEGO has finally revealed its Super Mario range that will include minifigures for the first time, including playsets for Bowser's Castle and numerous Mario Kart vehicles. Super Mario has been appearing in LEGO sets for years, though mostly as part of the company's bigger-scale range designed to work with the interactive Super Mario toy unit. That experiment now seems to over, however, with the long-awaited rollout of Super Mario sets scaled to minifigure size. And indeed, these will also include a growing range of Mario minifigures, with Luigi, Peach, Toad, Yoshi, Koopa Troopa, and Bowser Jr. all glimpsed in this first wave, as well as a Bowser big fig. The range will all be available from January 1, 2027. The range begins with Mario's Pipe Jump (72052), a 61-piece set priced at $9.99 that features a Mario minifigure, dinky Goomba element and large green warp pipe. Next up is Racing with Mario (72054), an 84-piece set for $14.99 that features a Mario minifigure and the plumber's classic kart. Green and red shells are also included, as is a banana.

item.title: Atari has today announced a new physical game collaboration with Activision called the Atari x Activision Collection, reuniting Activision with Atari after almost 50 years.
item.description: Atari has today announced a new physical game collaboration with Activision called the Atari x Activision Collection. The unexpected project reunites Activision with Atari after almost 50 years. The full set of working, physical game cartridges includes 39 classic Activision games, like Pitfall!, River Raid, and Kaboom!, and there will be three ways to purchase them. Individual, “Standard Edition” versions of 12 of the games will be available from November for USD$35 each. The 12 games include Pitfall!, River Raid, Megamania, Enduro, Kaboom!, H.E.R.O., Pressure Cooker, Private Eye, River Raid II, Keystone Kapers, The Activision Decathlon, and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns (although Atari notes The Activision Decathlon and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns will actually ship at a later date than the other titles). The Standard Edition games feature full packaging and a printed, colour manual inspired by the original releases. They’ll be compatible with Atari 2600+ and Atari 7800+ consoles, as well as original Atari 2600 and 7800 hardware. There will also be four box sets available, which will widen the collection to the full 39 games. The first of the four box sets (which are dubbed Treasure, Speed, Secrets, and Victory) will be available from late November, with the remaining three will follow over the first three quarters of 2027. These will be available via pre-orders at atari.com for USD$250. A complete collection of all 39 games (which will reportedly include a yet-to-be-announced “collectible item”) will also be sold via pre-order for USD$1000.

At gamescom 2026, Kabam and Herobeat Studios revealed a brand-new gameplay trailer for Wilderings that unveiled a fiery new Volcanic biome, a first look at Röhe the Moth Boss, and the confirmation that the open-world action-adventure game will be launching its Version 1.0 update in spring 2027. Wilderings, which also encourages exploration and features fast-paced action, roguelite progression, and creature collecting, follows Abi and her companion Rif as they traverse a fractured world that is quickly being consumed by darkness. To help in her journey, she will discover and adopt mysterious creatures known as Hântu, which she can use to help her fight, get through tough spots with their abilities, and to move about the world. In this new Volcanic biome, Abi will run into at least three Hântu, Razzle (explosive projectiles that burn and multiply), Mokul (summons pyroclastic rain that scorches an area), and Furioso (throws magma that spreads between enemies). As for Röhe, this Moth Boss is actually a young hunter from the Frostlands who will challenge Abi in this new region. To make it through the test set in a "magma-lit arena," Abi will have to perfet her movement, combat skills, and Hântu abilities.

item.title: Xbox design chief Carl Ledbetter reveals how an Ikea bookcase inspired the console’s design, as Xbox and Ikea launch the new YXSTABY furniture line.
item.description: Gamescom kicks off today in Cologne, Germany, and among the many big game debuts, hands-on demos, and major announcements is a new kind of reveal: Xbox is partnering with Ikea to sell an exclusive set of Xbox-inspired furniture and accessories that you can buy starting this fall. But, according to Xbox, the new collection goes far beyond the typical gamer chair and desk setup. Carl Ledbetter, head of design at Xbox, has been at Microsoft for more than 30 years (dating back to the days of the IntelliMouse) and is responsible for designing consoles like the Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S. Ledbetter led the charge with the Ikea collaboration and says the partnership isn’t as unusual as you might suspect . I spoke to Ledbetter exclusively at gamescom ahead of the reveal of YXSTABY (get it?) a “nine-piece collection designed for gaming at home,” and found out that Xbox’s ties to Ikea go back further than you might expect. “The piece of furniture that we use as our de facto test for any console design is the Billy bookcase from Ikea,” Ledbetter says. “So believe it or not, it's a natural fit. I’ve spent all my time [at Xbox] looking at input, controllers, the console, how things fit into the home. [That] matters when you design a console, [the] horizontal and vertical position. [So] this goes back years. The philosophy that we share for designing products at Xbox and at Ikea are nearly identical. So it was like a love connection.” IGN can exclusively reveal a look at the entire collection, which features nine pieces, including chairs with console pockets, thumbstick-shaped stools, a D-Pad inspired platter to hold your controller, X-shaped pillows, and more. Ledbetter says that planning a series of pieces intended to be picked up, sat on, leaned against, and otherwise interacted with came with a surprising challenge.

item.title: Konami is partnering up with a celebrity kitty named ‘one-eared Uno’ to debut a special Metal Gear cat toy collection available at CatCon 2026.
item.description: Konami is partnering up with a celebrity kitty named ‘one-eared Uno’ to debut a special Metal Gear cat toy collection available at CatCon 2026. If you didn’t know there was a cat convention, now you do. CatCon is a yearly event that brings together cat lovers from all over the globe to Pasadena, California, featuring special exhibits, workshops, adoption drives, and meet-and-greets with celebrity cats. One of those cats, affectionately named ‘one-eared Uno,’ and her owner, Kat Curtis, will host a special meet-and-greet event at the Konami booth at CatCon this year to celebrate the release of some special Metal Gear-themed cat toys. These offerings include cat scratch boxes modeled after the iconic cardboard boxes that Big Boss and Old Snake use to sneak around without being detected by enemies, plush pet toys, and even cat collars inspired by Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker and Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots.

The first of the Series 6 Magic Puzzle Company puzzles is now available to buy at Amazon and Target. The Spooky Shire isn't even listed on the company's website yet, so it appears to be making its retail debut a bit early. The Spooky Shire features original art from Kasey White and depicts a colorful scene full of ghosts, witches, skeletons, and a ton of cute little pumpkins. Like all Magic puzzles, it's made up of 1,000 pieces. If you aren't already familiar with the Magic Puzzle Company, It's pretty easy to explain why its one of the best puzzle brands out there. The pieces are unique, the art is always incredible (not AI generated), and there's always a magical surpise waiting for you at the end. These puzzles are also just really fun to put together. There's so many different things going on in each scene, which makes every newly added piece feel special. According to the product page, there are over 50 easter eggs to find as you put the puzzle together. You also get two art posters you can use as a reference.

item.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Songs of the Past expansion got a proper reveal trailer at gamescom Opening Night Live 2026, and developer CD Projekt Red showed up to talk about its new chain weapon, the realm of Letten, and more.
item.description: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Songs of the Past got a proper reveal trailer at gamescom Opening Night Live 2026, and developer CD Projekt Red showed up to talk about its new chain weapon, the realm of Letten, and more. Geralt of Rivia helped close out ONL 2026 when the studio talked about how it plans to revisit its critically acclaimed 2015 RPG with new content next year. There's still much that hasn't been revealed, but this first showing finally teased what it will be like for players to revisit The Witcher 3 12 years after its original launch. We'll get into all of the details that CD Projekt Red had to share, but first, the show had another surprise for viewers: a trailer. You can see the first The Witcher 3 Songs of the Past teaser below. So, what does the first Songs of the Past trailer tell us? Unfortunately, not much – at least at first glance. Geralt can first be seen approaching a tree decorated with lanterns before dancing in a camp with a partner who may not actually be there. Next, we're introduced to the moonlit skies and sun-kissed fields of Letten, the new realm where Songs of the Past takes place.

item.title: Shortly after Microsoft announced a translucent green Xbox Series X, Razer joined in on the fun with a collection of Xbox-themed gaming mice and keyboards.
item.description: With Gamescom and the 25th anniversary translucent green Xbox Series X on the horizon (for those with the cash to nab one), perhaps it's time to start looking around for similarly see-through accessories. So, of course Razer has announced new Xbox 25th Anniversary Edition versions of its BlackWidow V4 75% Mechanical Gaming Keyboard, Basilisk V3 Pro 35K wireless gaming mouse, and Hammerhead V3 X Hyperspeed low-latency AirPods-like wireless earbuds. These are the same devices we've come to know in the past. IGN called the BlackWidow V4 75 Razer's "most thoughtful" keyboard back in 2023; it's a less featureful version of the BlackWidow V4 75 Pro that sits on IGN's best gaming keyboards list. Like the existing V4 75s, the Xbox 25th Anniversary Edition features RGB lighting and hot-swappable keys, only now it's got a see-through green shell and keys, as well as a Razer and Xbox 25 logo-emblazoned wrist rest. Also, at $210, it costs $20 more than plain black or white models, and $10 more than other versions, like the existing translucent, but slightly darker-colored Phantom Green. Then there's the $180 Basilisk V3 Pro 35K mouse and the $120 Hammerhead V3 X Hyperspeed earbuds. The Basilisk V3 Pro 35K can work wired, but also works over Bluetooth and ships with a Razer HyperSpeed Wireless Dongle, and should be good for up to 210 hours of battery live via Bluetooth.
